title: A Stack With an Increment Operation

concept.title: Lazy updates: remember the increment, apply it when it is needed
body: You need a stack with a maximum size and an extra operation, `inc k v`: **add `v` to the bottom `k` elements** of the stack. Doing it element by element costs O(k) every time. The trick is to be **lazy**: store the increment in a helper array `add[i]` that means "add this to the element at index `i` **and to everything below it**".

For `inc k v`, let `i = min(k, size) - 1` and do only `add[i] += v`. When you **pop** the top element at index `top`, its real value is `value + add[top]`; then **pass the increment down**: `add[top - 1] += add[top]` (the elements below get it too) and reset `add[top] = 0`.

body.code:
push x:   if size < maxSize: vals[size] = x; add[size] = 0; size += 1
inc k v:  if size > 0: add[min(k, size) - 1] += v
pop:      if size == 0: -1
          else: size -= 1; result = vals[size] + add[size]
                if size > 0: add[size - 1] += add[size]
                add[size] = 0

body: Every operation is O(1). The same idea (store the change, apply it when you actually read the value) is used in many data structures, for example in segment trees.

statement: Implement a stack that holds at most `m` numbers and process `n` operations. Each line has three words: the operation and two numbers (unused numbers are 0). `push x 0` puts `x` on top if the stack has fewer than `m` numbers (otherwise it does nothing). `pop 0 0` removes the top and prints it, or prints -1 if the stack is empty. `inc k v` adds `v` to each of the bottom `k` numbers of the stack (or to all numbers if the stack has fewer than `k`). Print the result of every `pop`.
inputFormat: Each of the next `n` lines has an operation and two numbers.
constraints: There is at least one `pop` operation.

examples.input:
7 3
push 1 0
push 2 0
inc 2 100
pop 0 0
pop 0 0
push 3 0
pop 0 0
examples.note: After inc the stack is 101 102; pops give 102, 101; then 3.

hints: Do not add to k elements one by one.
Keep an array `add` where `add[i]` is to be added to the element at index `i` and everything below.
When popping, add `add[top]` to the value and pass it on to `add[top - 1]`.

starter.python:
import sys
input = sys.stdin.readline

n, m = map(int, input().split())
ops = [input().split() for _ in range(n)]

# Your code here

explanation: An increment is stored once at index `min(k, size) - 1` and meaning "this element and all below". It is applied when an element is popped and handed down to the element below.
